prep: Know your barangay evacuation center and route
Keep a go-bag: water, food 3 days, meds, flashlight, IDs in plastic
Move valuables and power off mains before water rises
Never walk or drive through floodwater (leptospirosis, currents)
Follow PAGASA Tropical Cyclone Wind Signals
Secure roofs, trim branches, store water
Charge power banks; keep a battery radio
Evacuate early if told by LGU
Duck, Cover, Hold
Anchor heavy furniture; know exits
After shaking, watch for tsunami signs near coasts: move to high ground
Join PHIVOLCS / NDRRMC drills
El Niño: conserve water, fire safety, heat stroke care
La Niña: more rain, flood and landslide risk
Farmers: follow DA/PAGASA climate advisories
Amihan (NE monsoon, ~Nov–Mar): cooler, rough seas east side
Habagat (SW monsoon, ~Jun–Sep): heavy rain west side, floods
Check gale warnings before sea travel
Store clean water (≈ 4 L/person/day guide)
Boil or treat water after floods
Fix leaks; harvest rainwater for non-drinking use
Keep flashlights & power banks charged
Unplug appliances during outages and surges
Generator only outdoors (carbon monoxide)
Respect marine protected areas and no-take zones
No single-use plastics on the beach
Heed small-craft/gale warnings

note: Guides are general preparedness tips summarised from common PAGASA/PHIVOLCS/NDRRMC guidance. Always follow your LGU and official advisories.
